title: Getting to know C++
note: Strings only. The step ids must match lesson-01.json.

why-cpp.title: Why a drone needs C++
body: On a Mars drone every millisecond counts: a command that arrives late is no longer a command. That is why drone software is written in a language that works directly with the processor and memory.
C++ is that kind of language. It asks more of the person writing it than Python does, and in return it gives speed and full control over what the machine actually does.

first-program.title: Your first program
body: Every C++ program starts with the function main. Everything inside it runs in order, from top to bottom.
first-program.caption: std::cout is the output stream — whatever you send into it appears on screen.

how-it-runs.title: What happens after you press Run
body: A C++ program cannot be executed straight away. First the compiler translates the text into machine code, and only then does the computer run it. If the text contains a mistake, the compiler stops and nothing runs.
how-it-runs.caption: Code → compiler → executable → output.

watch-intro.title: Watch how it looks
body: Two minutes on how a single line of text turns into something happening on screen.

predict-output.title: What appears on screen?
body: Two output statements, one after the other. Think before you answer.
predict-output.explain: std::cout adds nothing of its own. A space or a line break appears only if you write one.

fix-error.title: Find the mistake
fix-error.task: This program does not compile. Find what is missing, fix it and run it.
fix-error.hint: Every statement in C++ ends with a semicolon.

write-own.title: Write it yourself
write-own.task: Make the program print the number 42. Nothing else is needed.
write-own.hint: A number does not need quotation marks.

recap.title: What you now know
points: A program starts at main and runs from top to bottom.
std::cout prints exactly what you give it and nothing more.
Every statement ends with a semicolon, otherwise the compiler stops.
Compile first, run second — that is how C++ differs from Python.
